**First working version: your phone and Linux computer pair and stay connected.**

### What works
- **Pair by QR code.** Open Continuum on the computer, click *Pair a Phone*, scan the code with the app.
- **Always connected, nothing to open.** After pairing, both sides reconnect by themselves:
  after reboots, when you come home to your Wi-Fi, or when the computer is switched back on.
- **Phone battery on the computer** (level and charging), live.
- **Remove a device** from either side; the other side forgets it too.
- Encrypted end to end (TLS 1.3 with pinned keys). No accounts, no cloud: nothing leaves your network.

### Install
**Phone** (Android 10 or newer): download `Continuum-0.2.0.apk` below, open it, and allow
installing. When pairing, allow *Nearby devices* (needed on Android 17 to reach your computer)
and notifications. On Xiaomi/Redmi/POCO phones, tap *Open Autostart settings* in the app and
turn Continuum on, so the phone doesn't close it in the background.

**Computer** (Linux with GNOME, from source for now; a Flatpak comes later):
```
git clone https://github.com/sharjeelmazhar/continuum && cd continuum
scripts/setup-dev.sh --no-avd && scripts/install-desktop.sh
```

### Not yet
Sending files, clipboard, notifications and calls come in the next versions.
Android 8–9 support and pairing without a camera (6-digit code) are next on the list.

`Continuum-0.2.0.apk.sha256` lets you check the download.
